prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision and record
- Pledge to “stick with the plan” for economic stability, lower taxes, controlled immigration, stronger defence, and community pride.
- Claims since 2010: 4m more jobs, tax cuts for 29m workers, Triple Lock for pensioners, 2.5m+ homes, record police/teachers, biggest defence uplift since Cold War, Brexit delivered.

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no increases to income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: state pension and pensioner tax-free allowance both rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
- Childcare: 30 free hours from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; expand wraparound care.
- Child Benefit: move to household basis; phased withdrawal between £120k–£160k.
- Business: keep corporation tax; extend full expensing to leasing when affordable; 10‑point SME plan; cut red tape using Brexit freedoms.
- Infrastructure: redirect £36bn HS2 savings to regional transport; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G for all populated areas.
- Trade: complete FTAs with India/GCC; build on TCA without CJEU alignment; CPTPP accession; protect NHS/food standards.
- R&D/AI/industry: public R&D to £22bn; maintain reliefs; £1.5bn compute; £4.5bn for strategic manufacturing; back auto sector.

Welfare and work
- Tighten disability benefits (PIP) and work capability assessments; shift fit notes to work/health specialists; tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill.

Education and youth
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or part‑time civic service).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by curbing poor‑value degrees.
- Statutory ban on mobile phones in school day; parental transparency on curriculum.
- Advanced British Standard to replace A/T Level divide; English and maths to 18.

Borders and immigration
- Legal, annually falling cap on migration; higher salary thresholds; health checks and higher surcharges/insurance.
- “Stop the boats”: monthly removals to Rwanda; implement Illegal Migration Act; clear backlog; more returns deals; rewrite asylum rules internationally.
- Parliamentary cap on safe/legal routes based on local capacity.

Health and social care
- NHS funding rises above inflation; 92k more nurses, 28k more doctors; Pharmacy First, 250 GP upgrades, 50 more CDCs; 40 hospitals by 2030.
- £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door; AI diagnostics; federated data platform.
- Dentistry recovery (more NHS places; golden hellos; vans); new dentists to serve in NHS or repay training.
- Women’s health strategy; Cass Review implemented; mental health teams in all schools by 2030; expand Talking Therapies; cap social care costs from Oct 2025.

Crime, justice and extremism
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences (rapists serve full term; 25‑year minimum for domestic murders); new offences (spiking, deepfakes).
- More prison places; faster removals of foreign offenders; fraud crackdown.
- Stronger powers against disruptive/extremist protests; ban face coverings/pyrotechnics at protests.

Energy, climate and bills
- Net zero 2050 on “pragmatic” path: no new green levies/frequent‑flyer levy; keep bills/levies lower than 2023; energy efficiency vouchers.
- Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; two CCS clusters; SMR fleets and Wylfa nuclear; import carbon pricing by 2027.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes: brownfield fast‑track, urban densification, nutrient rules replaced with paid mitigation; protect Green Belt.
- First‑time buyers: permanent higher Stamp Duty threshold; new Help to Buy; extend mortgage guarantee.
- Renters Reform (abolish Section 21 after court reforms); leasehold reform; temporary CGT relief for sales to sitting tenants.
- Drivers: ban road pricing by councils/Mayors; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for new 20mph/LTNs; £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.

Defence and foreign policy
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; 5% of defence budget to R&D plus 2% exploitation; sustained support to Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and benefits.

Rural, farming, fisheries, environment
- Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament; UK food security target; 50% public food spend local/high‑standard; fast‑track farm infrastructure; extend Seasonal Worker scheme with taper.
- Renew £100m Seafood Fund; major flood defence; water company penalties/river recovery; trees/green access; deposit return; curb waste crime.

Union and governance; sex and gender
- Invest across Scotland, Wales, NI; protect UK internal market; implement Windsor Framework.
- Clarify Equality Act: sex means biological sex; protect single‑sex spaces and women’s sport; sex‑based NHS language; school/parental rights on gender.
